mainText:
A magnitude five point nine level election race tightens with less than two weeks to go, Air New Zealand warns of a three hundred and thirty eight million dollar loss, and the All Blacks have named their squad for the northern tour.

New Zealand.

Air New Zealand is forecasting a loss of three hundred and thirty eight million dollars this year, citing high jet fuel prices. The airline says it continues to manage its financial position carefully. This comes as Stats New Zealand figures show domestic flight prices for Christmas bookings are already up five point one percent on last year.

Advance voting is under way with less than two weeks until polling day. Act has published a manifesto promising twenty two billion dollars in cuts and has dropped an earlier migration promise. Chris Hipkins says a Labour led government would be formed by Christmas. The Greens have criticised billboards from the Sensible Sentencing Trust linking Labour and the Greens to gangs, calling them a new low, and have urged Christopher Luxon to condemn them.

A union backed report says private health providers received fourteen point eight billion dollars from Health New Zealand and ACC last year, eighty percent of the increase in public health funding. The report was produced by a coalition of health worker unions, some campaigning for a change of government. Separately, Waitākere's new six bed intensive care unit remains empty, with no staff, no operating budget and no opening date confirmed, reported by RNZ and the Herald.

In Western Bay of Plenty, Alan Kurtovich has confirmed his resignation as a councillor was driven by the district's Māori wards decision, triggering the current byelection. He says it was still the right call. In Kawerau, a man has had his sentence reduced over the manslaughter of a friend stabbed after a party, and may serve as little as two years.

Oil prices remain at their highest since May on reports the United States is again weighing strikes on Iran. The Reserve Bank's Official Cash Rate decision lands this week, with a twenty five basis point rise widely expected after petrol prices pushed up inflation.

World.

Lula da Silva has won a fourth term as Brazil's president, with incumbent challenger Flávio Bolsonaro disputing the result. Brazil's currency, the real, fell sharply afterward on investor concern about increased spending. A WhatsApp channel that drew more than ten million supporters is credited with mobilising Lula's online base into real world votes, reported by BBC and Al Jazeera.

Aleksandar Vučić's party has lost power in Serbia after twelve years, with celebrations in the streets following a vote driven by a student led protest movement. The outcome is being watched for its effect on Serbia's foreign policy direction, reported by BBC and Al Jazeera.

A US court has ruled that the Trump administration illegally fired Maurene Comey, a federal prosecutor and daughter of former FBI director James Comey. The judge found she was targeted because of her father, reported by BBC and Al Jazeera.

Technology.

Anthropic has filed for a stock market listing, warning in its own prospectus of catastrophic risk from artificial intelligence as it prepares to become the first major AI company to go public. The filing runs to three hundred and fifty five pages and discloses detail not previously public. Reported by BBC.

The global scramble over a critical flaw in the PHP programming language continues, now into its fifth day. Artificial intelligence tools helped uncover the vulnerability. The UK government has confirmed five hundred new vulnerabilities in its own systems, and Amazon says it was attacked before the flaw became public. The practical cyber event authorities feared has still not materialised, reported by BBC Technology.

Sport.

Rugby. Dave Rennie has named a thirty six man All Blacks squad for the northern tour, with Codie Taylor as captain. The squad features two uncapped players and eight players back from injury, including Leicester Fainga'anuku named as a loose forward despite being more often used as a midfielder or outside back. The All Blacks will also play Australia at the Melbourne Cricket Ground next year as part of the twenty twenty seven Bledisloe Cup series.

League. Rugby League World Cup. The Kiwis beat the Cook Islands eighty two to sixteen, a matter of record, capping a dominant day for New Zealand sides at the tournament. The Australian Rugby League has confirmed it will keep using the PNG Chiefs name in the NRL despite New Zealand Rugby's legal challenge.

Netball. The Silver Ferns have secured the Constellation Cup for the fourth time, fighting back in the final quarter against Australia. Coach Dame Noeline Taurua says the side is coming of age. Loose forwards Kaipo Olsen-Baker and Elinor-Plum King have been named finalists for World Rugby's Player of the Year award.

Golf. Ryan Fox finished in the top five on the DP World Tour event in Korea, three shots behind the winner. Dame Lydia Ko has denied social media claims she gave private golf lessons to South Korea's first lady, after being drawn into a political controversy there.

Basketball. The Breakers lost eighty six to eighty four to the Taipans in Cairns, a matter of record, and sit four wins and five losses on the season.

Rugby, domestic. Canterbury have defended their National Provincial Championship title, beating Northland after trailing twenty one to ten at halftime, scoring five second half tries to end Northland's unbeaten run.

Coming up. The Reserve Bank's Official Cash Rate decision this week. The Rugby League World Cup continues toward its semi finals. Election day is November the seventh.

End of flash.
